How to play on steam:

1. Go to the local files of the game
2. Delete Bin32 folder
3. Rename Bin64 to Bin32
4. Go into that folder you just renamed
5. Inside the folder rename Crysis64.exe to just Crysis.exe

Now the game will start. If you experience crashes then follow these extra two steps:

6. On steam go to the properties of the game and under set launch options type " -dx9" the space is important
7. Turn off all anti aliasing in game.

These are the steps I followed to make the game run most stable. I played for more than two hours with no problems. I heard people said that the gog version is stable but if you like me and got it on steam I hope this is helpful.

If you can find my user review for the original Crysis I noted how the quality of its level design seems to fall off a cliff later in the campaign. A lot of other people will probably tell you this too. Warhead feels as if Crytek made it specifically to address that problem. It’s pretty much a more tightly-designed package of Crysis levels with a couple new weapons and vehicles.

If you were actually interested in what the original Crysis game’s story was about I don’t know what to say, but Warhead’s is slightly better. It’s kind of like the difference between Predator and The Rock respectively, the latter being slightly less cheesy, but still bombastic in its own way. Warhead follows Psycho (the British guy) and features a somewhat decently played-out character arc between him and a new supporting character. That’s all I think I can really say about it.

Aside from the original game’s suit powers, a new grenade launcher, EMP grenades which weaken nanosuit-equipped enemies (who are far more common in this expansion) but you as well, drivable APCs, and a couple new kinds of mounted gun, Warhead’s selling point is its superior level design compared to the original game. Luckily the level designers managed to stay strong throughout. 

Crysis is a game that, behind its graphics, is hailed for open-ended mission design reminiscent of GoldenEye or Thief with huge maps. Ironically, almost all Warhead’s missions are pretty linear compared to the first game’s. But it manages to be linear without feeling like a Call of Duty-style corridor. It’s a very “wide” sort of linear.

The first mission ends with an open-ended base infiltration similar to some levels from Crysis, but after that everything is technically a straight line that still manages to give you a lot of options in how you play the game. The vehicle chase sequence immediately following that infiltration somehow doesn’t feel like a scripted event but instead simply has you follow a target within an open area. This is followed by what is, actually, a pretty well-done boss fight to contrast with the first game’s mediocre final boss. Afterwards there’s a section inside a battleship where Crytek actually manages to play some scripting tricks on you without automatically controlling the camera or putting you in a quick time event or anything. It’s almost more Half-Life 2 than Black Ops in this way. Warhead makes even its literal tunnels dynamic enough to let players have a say in how they tackle each combat situation, including a train section.

Visually, Warhead looks slightly better than the original Crysis but hasn’t had nearly as many mods made for it. Fortunately Crytek actually tried to optimize Warhead a bit so for most people the game should run better than Crysis. Warhead’s highest graphical features also aren’t locked behind DirectX 10.

Compared to the first Crysis, Warhead is kind of like the same meal with the same ingredients but prepared more diligently after the chef got some experience.

I have two personal stories with Crysis 1 and Crysis Warhead. First one is not really a story. It's more just a fact that Crysis 1 with Warhead was my first PC DVD retail copies ever. I was buying PlayStation 2 games before, but for PC they were first. I got them in supermarket and not in gameshop, during late 2008 with currency that doesn't exist no more (Slovak Crown) and during times when inflation basically didn't exist over here in my country, where only games and movies had prices of the Western World. To give you comparision, so you can imagine that - range of game prices used to be from 300SK as cheapest to 1999SK new ones. For 300SK you could easily have full varied food for weeks, even for a month. 

Second one is kinda rare. I saw Crysis 1 in 2007 on maximum settings running smoothly and looking stunning. It was not on any convention or expo, it wasn't in any gaming club. It was just next house to the right from ours. My schoolmate knew the guy that lived there, and he just told us that his older brother wants my schoolmate to go visit him (well, I was lucky bastard so I went with him also, uninvited, and before I saw that tropical island on the max settings I ate all of their fries with ketchup :D) And then I saw it. [h1]Words will never describe what kind of feeling it was, seeing that thing, without even knowing what it is, but to only know, that it's impossible.[/h1]

Well, enough of childhood sentiment, let's get straight into the Warhead. Released year later after first Crysis, [b]we're playing as Psycho, member of Raptor Team, destroying every Korean settlement on the opposite side of the island, while Nomand is catching chickens and turtles on the other side.[/b] In terms of graphics, game runs smoother, so I believe optimalization was done a little bit better. I had problems with the sound to be honest, cracked speakers, sound cut off, but when I used headphones, sound was working correctly, so it was error on my part.

While Crysis 1 will last you above 8 hours, also it depends on how you play it, and if you enjoy it, if you using slow approach, it can go up to 10 hours or so, with Warhead you will be done within 5/6 hours. I have feeling that some parts even outside caves might feel like a corridor, but almost every is just up on your approach. Also, infiltrating last airfield was super easy, and you could easily reach the container in stealth without notice. Yes, on hardest diff. 

I don't want to step into ending that much, just wanted to say that it wasn't good at all. Absolutely not. But it doesn't mean it's going to ruin your gaming experiences. Level-design is (at least for me) better than in first Crysis, and some levels really took my breath. I've liked the VTOL evac, in the middle of the game, after the running on APC.

To sum it up, Crysis Warhead is most definitely stunning brilliant game worth every single penny. It's younger brother of first Crysis and it's his lighter version. You'll enjoy every single moment out of the game. It's great FPS game, it's great stealth game and it's pumped up action with no brakes.

Crysis Warhead is the expansion pack for Crysis, or standalone expansion? I don’t know what to call it.
You play as Psycho, the Jason Statham-American who was in your squad during Crysis 1 and follows his adventures during that time. So now with Nomad busy being important, its up to you to fight a North Korean general guy that isn’t really important to the overall plot all that much.

I like his glasses, though.

Crysis Warhead is a shorter, more exciting game compared to its original counterpart. Clocking in at only 3-6 hours long depending on if you know what you’re doing or not, because of it this, Warhead just kind of turns everything up to 11.

From the get go, you’re fighting big boy battles against North Korean forces across the island, teaming up with Marines and other Nanosuit wearing buddies to shoot at NK soldiers and aliens. Its not a spoiler, you see one 10 minutes into the first game. 

Although sold as a kind of graphical power house, Crysis: Warhead actually has some neat stuff going on with gameplay, nothing to write home to your neglectful parents about, but its still fun. The nanosuit gives you ways to approach conflict or just avoid it entirely, meaning you can play the game as a balls-to-the-walls action game or a clunky stealth game if you really wanted to. 

The NKA or KPA or whatever they’re called have a kind of uniformity to them, I wasn’t even aware that they had classes until someone told me, and you can tell what they’re going to do just by looking at them. Each one of them has a job from entrenching to attacking to flanking to telling everyone what to do.
All of them get shot by me, so its kind of a wasted effort. 

Going into the Crysis Wiki, because that exists, there’s actually a lot going on under the hood. I’d be impressed if I didn’t just shoot all of them on sight. Or throw bricks at them. 

Warhead does a lot right compared to the original. You have more weapons to play with, more ammo for your main battle rifle so you don’t have to switch it out for the AK early on. Weapon customization returns as well.
I don’t know what else to say about weapon customization. 

Warhead also did the right thing by focusing more on the KPA than the aliens, though they’re still there, they’re still unpleasant to fight. Not because they’re hard, they’re just not fun to shoot at, breaking the one rule of video games that is “Shooting aliens=fun”

There was multiplayer at one point. It was called Crysis Wars and I remember playing it, it was fun. You could get enough points by playing the objective and killing enemy players to get a tank that fires nukes. I never got it, but I’ve been hit by it.

EA shut down servers for Crysis Wars back in 2014.  At the time of writing this review there are 7 people playing Team Fortress classic. Just thought that was interesting. 

Warhead was alright, but nothing to write home about. You’re basically getting a gimped game now that multiplayer is dead. Now, I’m not going to endorse [anything] but there’s still a way to sort of play Crysis Wars. Its kind of a big deal in some circles, its not really the same game.
You probably wouldn’t be interested. Unless you’re a Living Legend. 

Buy it for 5 dollars if you really need to play it, but just remember you’re basically getting half a game.

Crysis Warhead is a first person shooter, and is a standalone expansion top the original Crysis game. This was released in September 2008.

Warhead follows a side plot to the original story of "Psycho", an ally of the original protagonist, Nomad. You are thrown into challenges on the other side of the island at the same time as the original story.  One change with the gameplay that Warhead brings, is the chance to customize your weapons, allowing you to put silencers, different sights on, and other additions such as flashlights. All of the weaponry which was in the first game is still present here, with the addition of a few new guns such as dual wielding SMGs which are absolutely bad-ass.  We see the return of the super human style nanosuit too. 

Warhead features a optimized version of the Cry Engine 2, but it still lacks 1080P resolutions which is a real shame. The game still looks really nice and blows alot of recently released titles out of the water graphically, even though it is almost eight years old now. The graphics menu has interesting options available, you are basically having to pick the style of gamer you are; you get pigeon holed into categories such as "gamer" or "enthusiast" for example - to me this really doesn't look good. I should be able to pick the graphics options with their regular choices, and not some predefined garbage categories which we see here.  The lack of high resolutions slightly lets the game down. There is a hot-fix you can do by changing .ini file settings, but this also messes with frame rates, and lord knows what else. 

The story is a complete stand alone to the original game, you can play this game first and still be none the wiser that their is a prequel to it. I really like the idea that all of this story is going on at the same time as the original though, it makes the plot seem even deeper than before. 

Warhead has some well recorded voice acting, all be it a very generic English accent on the main character, but all of the other dialogue and sound effects are all very good. 

This game has various difficulties, much like the original. Playing on Delta mode, which is the hardest, will certainly give you a well worthy challenge if you are an experienced Crysis/FPS player, stick to the lower difficulties if you just want to see the story as enemies and gameplay takes a significant drop in difficulty. 

Warhead, much like Crysis 1, could sometimes be considered as an open world game. The levels which you are playing in, are absolutely huge. There are so many different methods of reaching the same location, that you can play this game exactly how you want it. I personally opted to try a more stealthy approach, and normally games don't really cater for different methods like that, but I was still able to experience everything the same. There are tons of little nuggets of extra story to find throughout each level too, from computers to checkout, to radio broadcasts of propaganda. Plenty of stuff to keep you looking in every building you come across. 

A full playthrough of Crysis Warhead will take you just about five hours; depending on how you play. My first run through was a regular all gungho all guns blazing playthrough, which took me just about four hours to complete. My second run, which was my stealthy approach, took me quite a bit longer. Normally I don't get as much enjoyment out of my second run through a game, but I was able to get the same, and if not more enjoyment out of a second playthrough, I was able to see a different side to the game which I didn't see before in the regular playthrough, and the higher difficulties add a little bit more replay ability too. 

As well as the aforementioned resolution issues I had. I did notice a little bit of screen tearing on the cut scenes. Turning on v-sync tanks the frame rate to sub 30, which is unacceptable. nVidia users can enable v-sync in their control panel but you will still get a bit of tearing sadly. I guess that's what you get from older direct 9 version of games when you are running more recent operating systems/direct x versions.

Crysis Warhead definitely stands the test of time when it comes to gameplay and story; it's hard to believe that this game is almost eight years old now. You wouldn't think so with the quality of the gameplay on show. It is a welcome addition to the Crysis franchise and one that should almost certainly be played by fans of the series, and just FPS fans in general.  For the low price of £7,99, you will be getting a significant length story mode, with plenty of replay ability with a very fleshed out story line to boot.

[h1] Why You Should Consider Playing Crysis Warhead? [/h1] 

If you liked the original Crysis then you're gonna love Crysis Warhead! This is hands down one of the best action shooters of the last decade. To those who disliked Crysis due to its slow paced mission progression should find this game much more enjoyable. For starters this is a standalone expansion title and a PC exclusive to Crysis from EA!! That' really something!

Crysis Warhead addresses almost every criticism from the main game. This is a very fast paced action shooter and I enjoyed every minute of my 7 hour campaign. Crytek engine has been updated and optimized so now Warhead not only looks better but runs better as well. 
Overall it was like playing a action blockbuster movie. The soundtrack is also top-notch and really pumps up the action. You'll love it as soon as you see the intro cinematic!!

The gameplay and combat remain nearly the same. Missions and environment are much varied, Crytek also took full advantage of driving. The enemies especially the aliens are much more stronger now and the A.I responds in a much better way. The graphics are just breathtaking as well. Keep in mind it's still a 12 year old game as of writing this review so don't expect it to look like a modern Call of Duty.

My only con is that it's criminally short but remember kids quality over quantity is what you get here! Also the standalone multiplayer expansion is long dead since termination of Gamespy service so don't throw negative reviews because the multiplayer is not working. There's nothing the developers can do 12 years later. 

So should you buy Crysis Warhead? Absolutely hell yeah!! Every FPS fan should play this cool adventure! It's really underrated and overshadowed by the Crysis 2 and 3 but maybe its because its considered as an expansion pack. It's okay....I guess? Regardless what I say, try it for yourself and let me know how you felt playing it.

Crysis Warhead. A standalone expansion. Set of missions, based on the first Crysis game. There we have a new main character, and supposedly some "other side of the island", with a different landscape and chain of events. At the start of sales, it was priced cheaper than the original Crysis game, and it was a valid point: there is the same engine, it's short (original Crysis wasn't that long, but Warhead is about 40-50% shorter). Most notably, a good half (if not 80%) of locations were in the original game, and were only slightly remade, to look different. As a good "pro" point, there was a "Crysis Wars" multiplayer, which was disputably better than in the original Crysis. But, multiplayer is dead at moment, so I'll write about the single-player campaign only.

Today the game sells at the same price as the original - 18$ (4.5$ with 75% discount). However EA does not adapt prices for various regions, and in my country Warhead costs as half of Cyberpunk 2077 or any other AAA release. And that's a serious reason not to recommend this buy, at least to my fellow countrymen. But it's not the main thing!

If you check negative reviews, you'll see that many players had difficulties with starting Warhead on their Windows 10 PC "out of the box", without tweaking. Well, good thing is that that issue was patched, and now you can play the game straight after installation, how it should be. I've only one middle game crush to OS, which is a really good result for that engine.

My reasons to downvote Crysis Warhead are more personal and biased, so it's ok if you're not agreeing with it.

For starters, the story is really worse than in the original game - despite the fact that the developers surely invested enough in that part, despite that we have there more deeply developed main character and a bunch of cutscenes, plus some "behind the scenes" drama between our man Psycho and his old fellow O'Neill... It's all the way more generic, more unbelievable, more out-of-any-sense. O'Neill was kicked out of Spec Ops, but have all credentials to fly hi-tech jets and VTOLs; is that's the way US military operates? They take unreliable persons to drive such things? Hmm. What's more, Koreans in this standalone expansion are surely even dumber than in "Homefront" games. A big turn around, actually, because they weren't like that in original Crysis.

There we go from the story to the missions development and to the balance of difficulty. In the original Crysis, we had on average more spacious mission maps, and despite that, the enemies were situated much better almost every time. In Crysis Warhead, there was much less product polishing. As a result, just the same enemies, in the game from the same developer on the same engine, became much more stupid in all of their actions. They just don't have enough script strings, as it seems. And to make it even worse, the developers are going into experiments with widely mixing aliens and Koreans as enemies during some missions. Do I need to say that those missions are quite script-lacking? Oh boy, it's a seriously, Seriously undeveloped in technical perspective game. There Koreans, all of sudden, have broad access to gauss guns, and even to the super high-tech of all that US military science has to offer, the end game gun which was theoretically only a single working prototype during the original Crysis. But, for the sake of game balance, all of their most advanced infantry units in nano armor, will be using only SMGs and shotguns!

I can call other lesser things for a whole hour, but I only want to share a general impression. Crysis Warhead is but a cheap standalone asset of missions, about the same quality that was produced after the release of the Far Cry 1 game by some amateurs using the Crytek SDK. Sure, the developers added some story - but it only makes the general game lore much less believable. "Character exposition" is looking cool only if you were raised by some comic-book-adoring cultists, and never ever tried to use logic in your life. The timeline of events is seriously inverted as if there were some little teneting Nolan in the development team. Mission maps are mostly looking exactly the same as in the original Crysis or only slightly refurbished. 

All in all, Crysis Warhead was supposed to be a fine shooter for those who liked to run around a tropical island in a nanosuit, scattering Koreans along the way and kicking alien life forms buttends. Alas, I see a big downgrade on all stages, comparing to the original Crysis game. Especially while playing on the highest difficulty. Therefore, the mark is 5/10, and I don't recommend buying it even for 4.5$. For 1$ or less, maybe. But Crysis Warhead is certainly not a classy product which I will proudly display prominently in my games collection.

Even though it’s now 5 years old the game looks fantastic and has some impressive physics (apparently the CryEngine was updated for this). The story is adequate, given the limitations of a game such as this, and the voice acting is convincing throughout. [b]This is a long review, so if you want a brief summary of why I recommend [b]Crysis Warhead[/b] skip to [u]Results[/u] and read from there.[/b]

Crytek creates another epic continuation onto the Crysis series. Crysis Warhead offers an alternative story from the eyes of Physco another one of the nano-tech marines. 

[b]Story:[/b]
On the same island as the original Crysis Warhead starts the story with Sergeant Sykes, Physco, who is on a vital mission to capture Korean cargo. It is up to you and your friend O’neil to push through the forces of North Korea and aliens alike to complete your objective. 

[b]Campaign:[/b]
The campaign consists of approximately seven missions, which vary in length. The campaign lasts anywhere from around four to seven hours depending on your play method. The initial missions are before are against human AI, but as you progress the enemy shift begins to occur as you start fighting less humans and engaging more aliens. The enemies, weapons, and abilities are the same as the original meaning this expansion only adds new missions and story. Regardless the campaign is well planned and the levels keep you wanting for me. They offer  dynamic play-styles that allow you to choose your completion style. 

[b]Gameplay:[/b]
As in the original the gameplay varies based on your difficulty. I played Delta and noticed most of the game was more about utilizing my cloak ability and catching enemies by surprise. The enemies will fire in the same place if you cloak and run, but if you hide for a few seconds they tend to forget you even existed and continue on with their business. Realistically this game is pretty fun and the combat can be dynamic – if you’re looking for run and gun you’d probably want to play on an easy difficulty. On the other hand if you’re more into sneak and strike then I’d recommend going for a harder difficulty. The abilities are fun, but you’ll notice you tend to use some over others. I rarely found myself using speed or super-strength, but instead almost exclusively cloak and shields (which auto selects when cloak deactivates). 



[b]Hints:[/b][spoiler]
>If you cloak in mid battle and move prone most of the time you can avoid actually having to move as the enemies will be shooting above you.
>If you see a gun with an attachment you have make sure to drop your gun and exchange for that one. Otherwise you won’t unlock the attachment.
>The Plasma Accumulator Cannon only fires a short range then explodes sending missiles outwards.  This means to really damage your enemies you need to get close to them. 
>IF you use a flashlight or a laser and cloak they can give away your position.[/spoiler]

[b]Results:[/b]
All and all Cyrsis Warhead is a great addition to the series and even if you didn’t play the first Crysis I would recommend giving it a go. It doesn’t really ruin any elements from the original if you play them backwards, but adds more depth to your Physco who in the first game seemed rather annoying. The campaign offers great complexity and amazing new environments. The graphics are of par to the original, annoyingly not 1080p, but still it looks good enough that you couldn’t tell anyway. I’d definitely recommend this game for someone who loves FPS games.

This is an expansion for Crysis, that covers the events happening to the character Psycho (who was absent for most of its story). There's little point playing this standalone game (it doesn't require the original game to run) if you haven't played Crysis, so for the purposes of this review I'm going to assume you're familiar with it.

First off - you don't need to play this to get any more of the plot, as it doesn't really add anything. Seeing as how the aliens are a known quantity it doesn't hold back on revealing them like the main game did, and they don't take long to show up.

Gameplay wise it's very much in the vein of the last half of Crysis - pedal to the metal action, with a fusion of the open ended approach of the original to more defined set pieces. Oddly enough it's miles better than Crysis at doing that, with some great levels that offer a pleasant mix of relatively freeform shooting, but on a somewhat more linear path than the first game. Then there's very linear set pieces, like one set on a train where you're using mounted gun emplacements to shoot various enemies, that are boombastic and exciting - something that couldn't be said about Crysis for the most part IMO.

It's still freer than the likes of Call Of Duty or Battlefield, but if you're hoping for the totally open approach of Crysis then you will be disappointed. Personally I thought Crysis didn't make much of that approach, so this game is a welcome refinement. Your abilities still don't add much to the gameplay, but that deficiency is lessened by the increased tempo of the action. 

Unfortunately, as a consequence of this focus, it's fairly short. There's no fat here, no chewy bits of gristle - just prime steak, albeit no doubt overly expensive prime steak back in the day. I finished this in 6 hours...on the second to last difficulty level. Now, it's less than a tenner in 2018, so that's not bad value. But back then - no sir, I don't like it!!. I think then it would have got a kicking, despite the quality it's just not long enough for a higher price. 

With it being much lower I have no qualms about recommending it. It's fun, and it still feels different from most games, and in truth it's possibly a bit more enjoyable than Crysis 2 or 3. However I haven't played them in a while to really verify that.

Graphically it's still nice, though you can easily see the compromises they've made to "optimize" this from Crysis. It's debatable if it runs better, since that's a moot point ten years later (i.e most likely running on more powerful hardware than at the time of release).....I had no issues playing either at a steady framerate, though I did notice a few bugs and glitches with Warhead. Overall it's worth a punt if you're late to the party.

EDIT: One final note - the controls on a pad are much more sensible this time around. Whilst it's still an annoying faff switching weapons, they have at least put things like iron sights / run / crouch on more sensible buttons than before. It was that bad in Crysis that it's worth mentioning here, if that's how you play of course....

The most immediate strength of Crysis Warhead is the gunplay. Whilst the game is a recognized technical marvel in terms of its visuals, the complexity continues into the shooting mechanics which feature bullet physics, wall penetration, gun-sway, damage location multipliers, and satisfying recoil. Guns hit hard, and can wipe out enemies in only a few bullets, but skill and precision are required to handle these to their full effectiveness. As you progress through the game your shot timing, recoil management, movement and on-field tactics all improve leading to you genuinely becoming a better player.

One area that surprised me was just how fun vehicles were to fight against. You're equipped with mines, claymores, C4 and missile launchers to destroy APCs, tanks and helicopters. However, my favourite moment was when I (accidentally) shot a small fuel canister on humvee, leading to its turret operator to be set ablaze and the driver to dismount the vehicle in a panic. The combat is addictive, skill-based and realistic.

On the other hand, Crysis Warhead’s story is a painfully generic and dull military spectacle led by your typical “bad-ass” British SAS soldier. At its worst, the game’s story borderlines on racist Western propaganda. I’m not one to draw a long list of contrived political interpretations from videogames, but when your main villain is a Korean called “General Lee” it gives you an idea of where its heading. The most egregious moment has to be when your character Psycho grabs a Korean, who blurts out a sentence in their native language, to which Pyscho responds “I’m British you bastard” in a thick East London accent. A death of a teammate falls completely flat considering we’re barely introduced to him, and Psycho’s reaction where he executes yet another Korean by drowning him lacks any sort of emotional vulnerability to create a powerful moment of loss and anger. 

Crysis Warhead give a better account of itself elsewhere. The visuals are even better than the original, and the excellent mouse optimisation means that you retain tight and responsive controls even when your frame rate inevitably dips. This makes performance drops feel much, much less impactful on gameplay and allows you to turn more of the settings up. The physics are also superb, with explosions propelling objects and dismantling structures with satisfying realism and weight. Firing an anti-tank missile at a decrepit beach hut and watching it cave in on itself, occupants inside, is fantastic without feeling comically exaggerated either.

Level design is strong too. Crysis Warhead works best when it’s either completely linear, or directly offers you multiple approaches. For example: battling through the inside of a frozen aircraft carrier is a spectacle of lighting, sparks and gunfire; whilst being tasked to infiltrate a wide-open military base gives you complete freedom to slip in the back or drive in guns blazing. Some areas offer an illusion of freedom, which is less convincing as it punishes the players attempts at creativity. For example, a hovercraft mission initially presents a wide-open map to drive around on but fallen trees and steep terrain actually force you on a very linear path. Crysis Warhead is best when it’s direct in its intentions. 

Crysis Warhead is also really short. Like, really short. I completed the game in 5 hours whilst on the harder difficulties. If I was on medium, I could easily imagine myself completing it in under 3 hours. For a cheap expansion pack that’s fine, but it does end rather abruptly, even teasing a final getaway which never comes to fruition. Overall, Crysis Warhead will provide fans of the series some extra entertainment, but is essentially a bonus mission pack that would I think should be bundled with Crysis 1 nowadays.

For anyone seeking more of the Crysis brand of open-ended military shooting, Crysis Warhead offers an interesting proposition. As much as I enjoyed the original game, the long stretches of hiking and occasionally frustrating battles made it hard to stick with at times. Warhead takes the core design in a slightly different direction, less focused on open maps and more focused on constant action. The result is something I found a lot more fun, if not as polished, than the game it’s ostensibly an expansion of, which is a rare feat in the realm of expansions.

Crysis Warhead follows the exploits of Nomad’s nanosuited squadmate Psycho as he fights through another side of the war. Falling between the assault on the harbor and the final confrontation in the original game, Warhead has you following a container loaded with a mysterious specimen that everyone is itching to get their hands on. You’ll butt heads with the North Korean forces under the fabulous General Lee as well as the alien forces (do they have heads?) spilling out of the island’s guts. The adventure will take you through valleys and mines and strongholds, as well as some ham-fisted backstory between Psycho and an old pilot acquaintance of his.

I appreciated the mounting tension and periodic reveals of the original Crysis, and in particular the focus on the mystery. Warhead tries to shoehorn in a bit too much drama, including one of those dumb scenes where the dude who just killed 800 people feels sick over offing one particular guy, and a cutscene battle between Psycho and his new nemesis that just comes off as awkward. It’s a good time to mention that the production values here are not up to par with those in the base game, with animations being rougher and cutscenes lacking that key cinematic quality. The game itself looks and runs as good as ever, but really the entire story side is pretty lacking.

Fortunately, the story isn’t at all the focus here. Crysis Warhead is built around action, near-constant battles against the forces between you and the container. Where Crysis let you sneak around hotspots or choose which objective to pursue, Warhead all but locks you into firefight after firefight. It feels much more linear but at the same time more structured for satisfying combat, like a Call of Duty game that’s not all manicured hallways. Your opponents are constantly changing too, pitting you against soldiers in one level and aliens the next, and then mixing the two for most of the back half of the game. Some of the impressive vistas are lost but you’ll be so busy running and gunning, you won’t have time to notice.

The weapons and enemies are all plenty familiar, though there are some neat additions in ammo types and smaller arms. The seven levels all lift pretty liberally from the base game as well (and I wish they had left the mine segment out) but there are some real stand-outs like a hovercraft chase across a frozen coast and a train defense mission. It’s not a long game, clocking in between three and four hours to pound through, but it feels like it crams almost all the action of the original into it. And ultimately that’s what I like so much about it, it takes the best parts of Crysis and cobbles them together into a new little kitbashed title. It’s very conspicuously an expansion, with all the production limitations that entails, but it’s one that comes from very good stock.

Crysis Warhead Review

I absolutely loved this game. For its time (around 2008, I think), it looked incredible. There isn’t much bullet drop or realistic physics, but that never bothered me. I played on Delta difficulty and had an amazing time—it felt like I was superpowered, but not invincible.

The stealth gameplay really stood out. Honestly, sneaking in this game felt better than in many modern titles. I had so much fun trying to stealth through missions, even though sometimes it felt like the game just knew where I was—like those older games that can magically detect you even when you’re invisible. In other areas, though, it was more balanced: enemies would only react if you got too close while cloaked, which felt a lot more realistic.

One thing that did bug me was how vehicles reacted when you were invisible. They’d sometimes stop or move awkwardly back and forth, almost like they saw you but didn’t want to go too far away.

The weapons were a blast—literally. The customization options were great, and you could approach combat however you wanted: full-on action or sneaky infiltration. Stealth was challenging (as it should be), but that made it even more rewarding. Driving vehicles and using different turrets depending on what you were in was also a ton of fun, though I did feel that enemy vehicles were a bit overpowered. Grenades didn’t do much against armored units—only rockets or mines worked, and mines were tricky to use without breaking stealth.

There was one cutscene that was supposed to be serious, but I couldn’t take it that way. My character was supposed to be mourning, but he kept making this weird grunting noise that honestly sounded like he was… taking a dump. It totally killed the mood and made me laugh instead of feeling emotional. Maybe it was a glitch, but it definitely broke the immersion for that scene.

The nanosuit powers were as awesome as ever. I loved the freedom to approach missions in multiple ways, and those overwhelming battles made it clear that while you’re powerful, you’re not unstoppable—you can still bleed, and you can die.

Fighting the Koreans in their power suits was tough since you could only really take them out with headshots. The helicopters were a huge pain too, but they made firefights feel intense and high-stakes. The aliens were even harder to hit and did heavy damage, but fighting them was still a blast.

The story was great overall, even though I noticed some issues—like facial animations not matching what characters were saying or doing. Everyone kind of had that “resting angry face,” and there were a few random audio glitches, like weird sniffing sounds. Still, the gameplay and story together made for an amazing experience.

The ending was fantastic—the epic showdown between your character and the General was perfect. I just wish it wasn’t only a cutscene; some close-quarters combat would’ve made it even better. Still, the villain was awesome—great design, believable motivations, and a strong presence. My only gripe is that Psycho had so many chances to kill him earlier but didn’t until the very end.

Even with its flaws, Crysis Warhead is an incredible game. The gameplay, story, and atmosphere all come together to make something unforgettable. I loved every minute of it.

This review is for the game ''Crysis Warhead'',a first-person shooter video game,developed by the video game company Crytek(Budapest).
The game was published by Electronic Arts and released in Semptember 16 on 2008(in North America) for Microsoft Windows.The game uses the CryEngine 2.The game is only available for Microsoft Windows.

Plot
You are Michael "Psycho" Sykes,a former British SAS Sergeant and member of the Raptor Team,a squad of mostly American soldiers who are invested suits with advanced technology.The story takes place on the other side of the island in which the original game <<Crysis>> is set and after you split up with Nomad(the main protagonist of the first installment) you go hunting the Koreans.Psycho has to engage through numerous of tasks and orders throughout the game in order to discover a container which envelops an alien war machine.You will have to secure that container(in some point you lose it)and kill a big bad alien (a Red Hunter) and you proceed to the exctraction.A last attempt (cinematic) is being made by Colonel Lee to accumulate the container,a fight scene follows but he fails and gets thrown off the ship leaving him to the mercy of a massive alien warship.O'Neill takes off with the container, as Psycho kicks back.

Character:As it has been stated you take control of a former British SAS Sergeant and member of the Raptor Team,Michael "Psycho" Sykes whom only from his code name (Psycho) you can understand that he is not the most conventional obedient military soldier.Even though he acts all tough and macho he does not take the life of a Korean(stating he was unarmed) and that wouldn't be fair.But as the story progress he watches his crew mate die helplessly,he snaps and kills by drowning a defenseless Korean soldier.After that he becoms a killing machine,always sticking to the mission and after he destroys the alien forces he successfully retrieves the container and leaves alongside O'neil having completed his mission.

Gameplay:Updated and refined gameplay of the original game.Newer graphics engine(CryEngine 2).Includes all the standart weapons from the original game with the addition of futuristic weapon builds,the introduction of Mini-SMGs which you can dual wield,EMP grenades and the PAX weapon which will be used on the destruction of the exoskeleton of the Red Hunter(last boss).


Multiplayer:The game comes with <<Crysis Wars>> ,a multiplayer mode.Even if this game is 6 years old you'll be surprise to see how many people still play crysis 1.

Recap:Like it's predecessor this game is a must buy.Breath-taking graphics,simple yet enjoyable story,challenging gameplay and exceptional first person shooter elements weave the greatness of this game.Only thing i dislike is that it's really smal.Took me only 6 hours to finish the whole game.I guess if you go around the map and kill everything it could last about 8-10 hours.Maybe more.

Thank you Crytek Developers for this wonderful game.

P.S If you are into the game's story you will like this game even more(like that's possible).Throughout the game you can listen audio clips from four years ago which explain a lot about the original game <<Crysis>> even about the successor <<Crysis 2>>.I am not going to say anything more.Buy the game,play it thoroughly and find out yourself :D

Dialog is kinda awkward because it was written originally in Hungarian afaik. And, might I add, the Hungarian version of the game is absolutely BRILLIANT in terms of dialog. If you can understand Hungarian and can get your hands on a Hungarian version of the game, I highly recommend going for it.

Crysis Warhead is a successful stand alone, which offers a more rhythmical campaign, richer and more dynamic than the original episode. Reverse of the coin: its linearity affects the diversity of approaches, which was one of the highlights of Crysis. So, the experience is somewhat less successful, especially since the surprise is not the same and its short life leaves  the player hungry. However, by offering many improvements and an enhanced multiplayer mode, Warhead remains an indispensable acquisition, especially at the price where it is sold.

The game itself is just fine. 

The issue is that the game doesn't run properly. Regardless of what fixes I try (and I tried different suggested fixes for most of two days) I can't get the game to run stable. If I'm lucky I'll see an hour uninterrupted, but more often than not I only get a few minutes between crashes. It doesn't matter if I have the game set to 4K/Max or 1080p/min, it's just a crapshoot. Eventually I had to abandon the game because at a certain point the game just won't run foe more than a few seconds.

So basically it's a good game that doesn't run.

[h1]Crysis: Die Hard Edition[/h1]
Warhead is a standalone expansion for Crysis 1 that follows the events of the first game but this time you play as Psycho (The British Dude, Basically Jason Statham). You run around the island as the aliens begin their attack all over the place with every weapon you could possibly need including the all new Dual SMG's. Guess we finally developed the ability for men to multi-task in this iteration.  

Story is ...passable because I enjoyed the gameplay.

More of an action shooter then the first with a few moments where it makes sense to stealth but its faster paced and quite a bit shorter at only 3-4 hours as compared to Crysis's 8-9 hours.

Enjoyable and obviously... still looks great. Though in this one the shading does seem to be a little flatter and the textures not as crisp. Feels a little rushed out.

A superb game! The suit is so damn fun to use. You'll do things like use invisibility to creep up on an unsuspecting Korean patrol. Changing to maximum armour, you ambush them with a well placed grenade and then finish them off. But now the Koreans have heard the noise and seen you, and are closing in to flank you. How's your energy? Can you hide behind cover to flick back to invisibility so you can invisibly creep to a different bit of cover, flanking your enemies as they close in on where they think you're still hiding? Or are they already too close, and you have to switch to speed and make a make a mad, desperate dash to avoid being killed? Or should you switch to strength and jump onto the roof of that building where they can't reach you? Or will someone lob a grenade at you and make the roof collapse? The open levels, suit powers, and weapon customisations give you so many possibilities. The combat is intense, brutal and visceral (best played on delta difficulty). And it's gorgeous. Awesome graphics are used to render intensely beautiful scences. The plot is standard action fare, but it's told with such visual flair and uses such beautifully atmospheric locations that I was still interested in it. The one issue I had is that there's now noticable pop-in, compared to the original crysis. And it's short but cheap. With this level of quality, I wouldn't mind long but expensive :) But it was still a 10/10 experience for me
